name: Suffolk
description: Suffolk is a largely rural county in eastern England known for farmland, picturesque villages, medieval wool towns and a long North Sea coastline. Ipswich is the main urban centre, while Bury St Edmunds, Southwold and Aldeburgh are notable historic and cultural destinations.

places.name: Mid Suffolk
places.description: A rural district of Suffolk market towns and villages, including Stowmarket and Eye, known for timber-framed buildings and gentle farmland.

places.name: Babergh
places.description: A rural district in Suffolk known for its picture-postcard wool towns like Lavenham, with some of England's best-preserved medieval timber-framed buildings.

places.name: Forest Heath
places.description: A former district in Suffolk covering Newmarket, the historic headquarters of British horse racing and home to the National Horseracing Museum.

places.name: Ipswich
places.description: The county town of Suffolk and one of England's oldest continuously inhabited towns, with a waterfront marina built from its historic docks.

places.name: St Edmundsbury
places.description: A former district in Suffolk centred on Bury St Edmunds, a medieval town named for the martyred Anglo-Saxon king whose shrine once made it a major pilgrimage site.

places.name: Suffolk Coastal
places.description: A rural, coastal former district in Suffolk covering the seaside town of Aldeburgh and the Sutton Hoo Anglo-Saxon burial site.

places.name: Waveney
places.description: A former coastal district in Suffolk covering the seaside town of Lowestoft, England's most easterly point.
